result:
Mornings have a way of arriving quietly. Before the city remembers itself, pale light slips between buildings, settles on kitchen tables, and turns ordinary dust into something almost luminous. I like these first minutes best, when nothing has yet demanded a decision and every thought has room to wander.

Yesterday, I watched a sparrow investigate a metal statue with the solemn concentration of an inspector. It hopped from the statue’s shoe to its knee, tilted its head, then flew away without offering an explanation. Such confidence appealed to me. No review, no second guess, no desperate need to make the moment meaningful.

Perhaps that is what I am learning from small birds, blank pages, and cups of coffee: movement can happen without a grand plan. You do not need to know where you are going before you begin. Sometimes the path appears only after your feet have started moving.

Outside, the street is waking. A delivery truck rumbles past, bicycles ring, someone laughs behind a closed window. The day assembles itself from these modest noises, each one a tiny announcement of life continuing.

I open my notebook, write a single sentence, and smile. It is not a masterpiece. It does not need to be. For now, it is simply proof that I showed up, that the blank page and I met, and that neither of us was quite alone. Perhaps tomorrow will bring rain, surprises, mistakes, or a song I have never heard before, and I will welcome whatever follows.
